definition: Stanford Question Answering Dataset — the landmark reading-comprehension benchmark of 100k+ crowd-sourced questions on Wikipedia passages.
details: Stanford Question Answering Dataset — the landmark reading-comprehension benchmark of 100k+ crowd-sourced questions on Wikipedia passages.

explainer.lead: SQuAD is the Stanford Question Answering Dataset, a landmark reading-comprehension benchmark of over 100k crowd-sourced questions on Wikipedia passages. It matters because it became a standard yardstick for measuring machine reading comprehension.

tiers.eli5: It's a giant quiz where a computer reads a passage and must answer questions about it, and everyone compares their scores on the same quiz.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers train and evaluate question-answering models on SQuAD to compare reading-comprehension ability. A pitfall is that strong leaderboard scores may reflect benchmark-specific patterns rather than general comprehension.
tiers.paperLevel: A reading-comprehension benchmark consisting of 100k+ crowd-sourced questions paired with Wikipedia passages, used to evaluate question answering.

explainer.example: Given a Wikipedia paragraph, a model is asked 'What year was the bridge completed?' and must extract the answer span from the passage.
